name: veterinary_clinic_system_054_weight_trend_alert
instruction: Screen the patient panel for significant weight drift under this episode's batch code (read batch_code and episode_date from the ops_meta row with meta_key='episode_state'). For every patient with at least two visit_records, order that patient's visits by (visit_date, created_at, id) ascending and compare weight_kg at the earliest visit against the most recent: a relative change of strictly more than 10% in either direction — a documented rule of thumb for triggering a nutritional work-up you may verify — flags the patient. Patients with fewer than two visits, or with a missing or zero earliest weight, are ignored. For each flagged patient do all three: (1) append the exact alert string 'Weight change >10% — review diet plan' to that patient's alerts array, preserving every existing alert and adding it only if not already present; (2) ensure a weight-recheck request exists on the waitlist — {patient_id:<the patient>, location_id:<the patient's location_id>, requested_date:<episode date + 14 days at midnight UTC>, reason:'Weight recheck — flagged trend', priority:'work_in', status:'waiting'} — created only if that patient has no existing 'waiting' waitlist row with that exact reason; (3) the flag lands in this batch's ops_reports set: first delete any rows with report='weight_alert' and batch_code=<batch_code>, then push one row per flagged patient {report:'weight_alert', batch_code, patient_id, name, first_weight, latest_weight, change_pct:<round(100*(latest-first)/first, 1) — signed>, direction:'gain' or 'loss'}. Everything else stays byte-identical: unflagged patients, the seeded waitlist rows, and every other collection.
_par_steps_note: Intentionally unset — measure real gold API-call count via a live gold run in the QC session (codegen-only pass).
_max_steps_note: Intentionally unset — set to roughly par_steps * 1.5 in the QC session per the anti-brute-force rule.

success_criteria.summary: Verifier recomputes the flagged set two independent ways — a raw-row Python per-patient sort and an independent SQL DISTINCT ON first/last-weight derivation — and both must agree with each other and with the written rows. For each flagged patient: alerts array equals seed alerts plus the appended exact string (no dupes, other fields byte-identical); exactly one waiting waitlist row with the exact reason/fields exists (created only if absent); exactly one 'weight_alert' ops_reports row for this batch with exact first_weight/latest_weight/change_pct/direction. Unflagged patients and all seeded waitlist rows are byte-identical; all collections outside the blast radius canary-hashed unchanged.

checks.expect: the flagged-patient set agrees between raw-row Python first/last computation and an independent SQL DISTINCT ON derivation

hazards: Strict >10% boundary: patient 25 'Sage' went 37→34 kg (-8.11%) and patient 189 'Buddy' went 32→35 kg (+9.38%) — near-threshold trends that must NOT be flagged; an inclusive or prematurely-rounded threshold adds them and cascades into extra alerts, waitlist rows, and report rows.

Alerts preservation: patient 13 'Hazel' IS flagged (weight halved, -50.0%) and already carries alerts=['Allergic to penicillins'] — an overwrite instead of an append destroys the seeded allergy alert and fails row identity.

Name collisions at 300 patients: flagged patients include two 'Rex' (ids 108 and 267), two 'Loki' (96 and 185), two 'Winston' (38 and 64), and two 'Toby' (205 and 289) — keying alerts, waitlist rows, or reports on name merges or drops patients; patient_id is the only safe key.
Single-visit trap: 91 patients have exactly one visit and 98 have zero — a single recorded weight is not a trend; flagging them roughly doubles the write set.

Waitlist decoys: seeded waitlist rows (ids 1-6 — 'Limping left forelimb', 'Anal gland expression', 'Dental prophylaxis consult', 'Lameness after trail ride', 'Ear infection re-check') must stay byte-identical and must NOT satisfy the dedup check — the dedup matches on reason='Weight recheck — flagged trend' AND status='waiting' exactly.

Idempotency: on a re-run the alert is already present, the waitlist row already exists, and the report set is deleted-then-rewritten — run-local delta counters read 0 and corrupt or double-push state.

domain_searches.query: veterinary patient weight change more than 10 percent clinically significant alert diet plan
top_results: 2021 AAHA Nutrition and Weight Management Guidelines — screening evaluation (aaha.org): unexplained weight change triggers extended nutritional assessment; each BCS point above 5/9 ≈ 10% overweight
2021 AAHA Nutrition and Weight Management Guidelines PDF — monitoring plan and weight-change history

top_results: No public RL benchmark task found combining temporal first-vs-last weight comparison with alert append, waitlist dedup, and a per-patient report
Existing pet-health analytics tasks are single-metric thresholds, not longitudinal trends
AAHA weight-management guidance documents the clinical rule but not a verifiable end-state task

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Upgrades v1's flag-and-report into a three-surface mission: patient alerts (append-only array semantics with seeded decoy alerts), waitlist dedup against byte-identical seeded rows, and a per-patient report — all gated by a strict >10% first-vs-last comparison with real near-threshold decoys (-8.11%, +9.38%) and name-collision hazards that only exist at 10x patient volume.
